He was also called up by Xavi Hernandez for his four games in charge of the Netherlands. item.title: Three well-known players you did not play for Barcelona and Alaves
item.description: Three well-known players you did not play for Barcelona and Alaves Barcelona and Deportivo Alaves meet in La Liga with very different ambitions , but their histories share an interesting connection through several players who have represented both clubs. While Barcelona’s identity is closely associated with its illustrious history and La Masia academy, Alaves have built their reputation through memorable challenges against Spanish football’s biggest sides. The connection between the clubs stretches across generations, and Barcelona’s own historical records list numerous footballers who have worn both shirts, including former internationals, academy graduates and players who made their mark at Mendizorroza. Three particularly recognisable names are Jordi Cruyff, Bojan Krkic and Denis Suárez. Jordi Cruyff played a memorable role in Alaves history Jordi Cruyff is arguably the most intriguing name on the list because of his connection to both clubs and one of Alaves’ greatest European achievements. Jordi Cruyff played for Alaves for three seasons. (Picture Credit: Gary M Prior/Allsport) The son of Barcelona icon Johan Cruyff, he developed through the Catalan club’s youth system before making his first-team breakthrough during the 1990s. The attacking midfielder represented Barcelona between 1993 and 1996, making 54 appearances and scoring 11 goals. After spells with Manchester United and a loan with Celta Vigo, he joined Alaves in 2000, remaining at Mendizorroza until 2003. His contribution to the Basque club’s memorable 2000/01 UEFA Cup campaign ensured his place in its history. Alaves reached the final against Liverpool, producing one of the competition’s most dramatic matches. Cruyff scored in the 89th minute to make it 4-4, although Liverpool eventually secured a 5-4 victory through a golden goal in extra time. Cruyff later returned to Barcelona in an executive capacity, serving as the club’s sporting director between 2021 and 2023. Bojan Krkic experienced two very different spells Bojan Krkic played at Alaves on a season-long loan. (Photo by Denis Doyle/Getty Images) Bojan Krkic was once regarded as one of the most exciting prospects to emerge from La Masia. He broke into Barcelona’s senior side as a teenager in 2007 and spent four seasons with the first team before beginning a career that took him across several European leagues. His connection with Alaves came in the 2017/18 campaign, when he joined the Basque side on a season-long loan from Stoke City. The move offered him an opportunity to regain regular playing time in Spanish football, although his involvement remained limited, making 13 La Liga appearances without scoring. Bojan eventually retired from professional football and returned to Barcelona in a different role. He became the club’s football coordinator in 2023, with responsibility for monitoring young players at La Masia, a position that he continues to hold to date. item.title: Real Madrid emerge as clear favourites to sign Manchester United wonderkid as Barcelona and PSG fall behind
item.description: Real Madrid emerge as clear favourites to sign Manchester United wonderkid as Barcelona and PSG fall behind Real Madrid have been linked with a potential move for Manchester United wonderkid JJ Gabriel for quite some time now. The club have been working to secure the signature of the 16-year-old, who is pushing for a move away from the English club. Now, according to Diario SPORT , Los Blancos have emerged as the clear favourites to sign the English youngster. Gabriel is said to have rejected PSG’s latest proposal, while Barcelona have also decided to withdraw their interest due to the financial demands. Real Madrid move closer to signing JJ Gabriel PSG recently submitted an improved sporting and financial proposal in an attempt to convince the teenager’s camp. However, the 16-year-old has rejected the offer due to his preference to continue his career in Spain. JJ Gabriel is considered a massive English prospect. (Photo by Naomi Baker/Getty Images) Bayern Munich had already abandoned their pursuit. With Barça also not moving for him, that leaves the road clear for Real Madrid. The report outlines that Los Blancos are willing to make a huge investment of over €10 million in a three-year package to bring the teenager to the Spanish capital. However, the deal is not yet completed. An exit arrangement with Manchester United still needs to be reached. Real Madrid could secure another exceptional talent Gabriel has been widely regarded as the single biggest English talent coming through the ranks in the Premier League. The England youth international impressed for Manchester United’s academy, scoring 20 goals in 21 U-18 Premier League games last season. He also netted a hat-trick on his UEFA Youth League debut in September. Even though he has just turned 16, he already plays like a much older player. Real Madrid could overcome significant competition to secure Gabriel’s signature . (Photo by Naomi Baker/Getty Images) Signing him would be a significant coup for Real Madrid, considering the kind of European competition they had to see off. His dribbling, creativity and goalscoring instincts suggest he can be moulded into a fearsome attacker in the future. Although the financial commitment is significant considering the player’s age, Real Madrid will be paying for potential. If JJ Gabriel develops into the player everyone thinks he will, the amount Los Blancos spend now will look like a bargain. It remains to be seen what steps remain before the Manchester United wonderkid becomes a Real Madrid player and how the negotiations play out.

item.title: What Is Behind The Business Spat Between China And Soccer Superstar Kylian Mbappé?
item.description: Kylian Mbappé featured in a Chinese advertising campaign. GETTY IMAGES A dispute involving between French soccer player Kylian Mbappé , who plays for Spanish giants Real Madrid, and China was triggered after Mbappé supposedly disparaging references to former Chinese leader Chairman Mao. Mbappé, known for his commanding presence on the soccer field, has long been the subject of viral internet memes branding the Frenchman a dictator. In such memes, his face is often superimposed onto that of recognizable autocrats, including Soviet leader Josef Stalin, Ugandan strongman Idi Amin and former Chinese Communist Party leader Mao Zedong. Responding to the memes on a French podcast called The Bridge, Mbappe said that he found the jokes which saw his face superimposed onto Mao's, who he refers to as "a Chinese dictator," the most amusing. Backlash was swift; the clip has since been taken down but Beijing has stopped broadcasting matches of the Spanish soccer league, La Liga, and Chinese social media Xiaohongshu has frozen Mbappé's account. Chinese companies Dongpeng, Mengniu and Milkground have also all announced that they were scrapping their commercial partnerships with the athlete. "My comment was ill-judged, and I now understand that it hurt many people in China and in Chinese communities around the world," Mbappé said in a statement on Tuesday,. La Liga and Real Madrid have also apologized in the aftermath of the controversy. "LALIGA deeply regrets the offence that Kylian Mbappé's recent comments have caused among Chinese fans ... respect, coexistence and unity among people of all cultures are fundamental values of Spanish football. Guided by these principles, we reaffirm our respect for China, its institutions and its people," the league posted in an official press statement on Tuesday. "Real Madrid C. F. wishes to express its apologies to the Chinese people for any discomfort that may have been caused by the recent words of our player Kylian Mbappé," the Spanish club also said on Wednesday. However, many Chinese social media users were unaware of what Mbappé had actually said, as censorship largely censored any mention of the footballer's specific criticism of Mao. Mao founded the People's Republic of China, of which he was Chairman between 1949 and 1959, after defeating the Chinese nationalists in the Chinese Civil War. He is revered in China, whose government cracks down on criticism of communist party leaders such as Mao. Although his leadership is associated with major developments of the Chinese economy from a war-torn agrarian state to a more modern, industrialized one, his policies and dictatorial rule are widely seen as responsible for causing the deaths of millions of people. item.title: Aston Villa to take legal action against Jamie Carragher over 'unacceptable insults'
item.description: Aston Villa are preparing to sue Jamie Carragher over comments he made about the club and its supporters. The row centres on remarks the former Liverpool defender delivered on the Stick to Football podcast, where the prospect of Unai Emery replacing Michael Carrick at Old Trafford was under discussion. Carragher had suggested Emery should consider taking the Manchester United job, and criticism followed. His response to Villa fans who criticised him was to tell them to “shut the f*** up”. The 48-year-old, now a Sky Sports pundit, argued that football operates with a hierarchy, saying “Aston Villa will never be Man United”. “I’m not trying to annoy Villa fans but there is a chain in football, whether you like it or not,” said Carragher. “So Real Madrid will take Man United’s best player, they’ll take (Cristiano) Ronaldo. There’s very few above United, the same with Liverpool. Jamie Carragher’s comments on the Stick to Football podcast have caused a stir (Richard Sellers/PA) Villa issued their response on Friday evening, posting a statement on X that was signed by chairman Nassef Sawiris. “Aston Villa will initiate legal action against Jamie Carragher for his unacceptable insults about the club and its fans,” the statement said. “Aston Villa will not allow anyone to stop our ascension in English and European football. Nassef Sawiris, Chairman.” Michael Carrick’s position is hanging by a thread (Martin Rickett/PA) (PA Wire) Meanwhile, Michael Carrick says challenging conversations and hard truths have been necessary as misfiring Manchester United attempt to end their worst winless run since 2015. Boos echoed around Old Trafford last Sunday after the Red Devils crumbled in a 3-0 defeat to Bournemouth that saw fans focus their fury on the club’s ownership, hierarchy and players. Carrick avoided such wrath as the United faithful acknowledged that their issues run far deeper than the popular former midfielder despite him overseeing an eighth successive match without a win. The 45-year-old, to the shock of many onlookers, will have the chance to turn the situation around at Chelsea on Saturday following a week that has required honesty and introspection. Under-fire head coach Carrick, who claimed he was not surprised to still be in charge and did not need assurances from above, said: “It’s not always rosy and nice conversations between anyone. “Whether that’s between me and the players, whether that’s between me, Jason (Wilcox, director of football), Omar (Berrada, chief executive) or the owners. “It’s the truth, it’s the hard truth at times, and it’s what we need to move forward. Whatever we need to move forward, we’ll do.” Carrick earned a two-year deal having led United to third last term but there is a sense that he has been given a stay of execution having won just two of 12 matches this season. item.title: 3 biggest takeaways for Sixers following NBA Cup win over Knicks
item.description: PHILADELPHIA -- The Philadelphia 76ers were able to open up NBA Cup play with a 98-93 win over the New York Knicks at home despite missing Jaylen Brown due to left knee tendinopathy. The Sixers improved to 5-1 on the season overall and are 1-0 to begin Cup play as they look to work their way out of Group B and advance to the knockout rounds. Tyrese Maxey led the Sixers with 27 points and four assists on the night. LeBron James added 20 points, nine rebounds, and eight assists, Joel Embiid had 10 points, seven assists, and seven rebounds, and VJ Edgecombe added 13 points and eight rebounds. Anfernee Simons hopped off the bench and poured in 21 huge points. Here are the three biggest takeaways for the Sixers following their win over the defending champs: Sixers lean on their defense The Sixers entered the night ranked third in the league in defensive rating and they flexed their defensive muscles in this one. Philadelphia finding a way to hold the Knicks to just 93 points and 40.7% shooting is impressive. The Sixers also forced 13 turnovers which they turned into 23 points as they were able to take advantage of New York's mistakes. All night long, the Sixers were tough on the defensive end, even when the Knicks would go on their spurts to make the game closer, Philadelphia would then settle on that end and shut off New York's water to close out the champs for the second time. "It’s been very, very good," said coach Nick Nurse of the team's defense. "I think that the half-court, especially, has been phenomenal because our starting and especially ending goes through some moments still, or getting it back and getting set up. And I thought we gave up a few too many second shots. But when it's set, the physicality, the communication, the keeping the ball in front, the really not quitting on plays, just not biting on fakes, not giving up angles, we made them take 10 shots where they were just stuck, and they had to throw up a turnaround and we still challenged it. So you have that many good defensive possessions in a game. That's going to take you a long way." Simons stays hot After knocking down six triples in Philadelphia's win over the Indiana Pacers, Simons knocked down another five against the Knicks. There were moments in the third when Simons stepped up and knocked down some huge triples in order to keep New York at bay and keep the scoreboard moving. The Sixers had gotten stagnant a bit on offense as the defending champs began to flex their muscles, but Simons hopped off the bench and drilled some huge hoops. Those are the types of plays Philadelphia acquired the 9-year veteran for. He was huge in the win. "Just reading the game, letting the game come to me," Simons said after the win. "Obviously, first half, offensively, for me was kind of slow but kind of stuck with it. You know, the guys got going. I was able to get some good looks. Everybody pretty much found me out there on the wing or in the corner, so I was able to get going through there.

item.title: A real surprise: Andoni Iraola has a new weapon and it makes Liverpool lethal
item.description: A real surprise: Andoni Iraola has a new weapon and it makes Liverpool lethal Liverpool didn't do Andoni Iraola any favours at the start of his time in charge. He's got a new weapon, though, and that changes everything. We're not sure it was a good idea to give Andoni Iraola zero natural right-wingers to start his Liverpool career. That's the job at hand, though, as the Reds let Mohamed Salah leave the club but never actually signed anyone to fill his role. And filling that role didn't necessarily mean 'focal point of the attack'. Liverpool have other players for that. It just meant signing someone who could naturally play on the right wing, given it's very much still a role that the team calls for. Instead, Liverpool provided Iraola with four left-wingers, all of whom are right-footed. That's not to say that none of them can play on the right but it's not their natural game and going on the outside of defenders to hit the byline isn't making the most of their skillset. Or at least, we didn't think it was. Iraola may have changed all of that, though. Andoni Iraola's new weapon Iraola has had to make do with what he's been provided, of course. That's the life of a 'head coach' who doesn't necessarily have a final say on incoming transfers. We'd argue he's done spectacularly well given the circumstances, too, as the Spaniard has essentially given himself a new weapon with some clever coaching. Rio Ngumoha has been a revelation on the right. The winger is naturally a left-sided player but Iraola has trusted him to change flanks this season . It's actually at the point now where Ngumoha might be better on the right, in fact. After all, he's not quite a major goal threat just yet and cutting inside merely offers some threat from Ngumoha, rather than an out-and-out concern for teams. From the right, though? He can make magic happen as a creative force. The cut-back is one of the hardest to defend attacks in football but requires players who can get right to the byline and inside the box. Sometimes movement and quick passing is enough to get that done but sometimes it needs an individual who can run at defenders and manoeuvre in tight spaces. Ngumoha showed he can do that, particularly against Villarreal where he was outstanding. His ability to stretch the opposition defence and turn them towards their own goal feels much, much more valuable than his cutting inside right now - and adds a dimension to this attack that Liverpool otherwise lack. That's all thanks to Iraola, who has done incredibly to work with a squad that didn't have a natural right-winger. It's starting to look like the role might be natural to one of them after all, though, and Ngumoha feels like a player transformed.

item.title: Alexis Mac Allister provides Liverpool contract update
item.description: Alexis Mac Allister provides Liverpool contract update Alexis Mac Allister Future Remains Open as Liverpool Contract Talks Stall Alexis Mac Allister has offered fresh clarity on his Liverpool future, while underlining that his contract situation remains unresolved despite another strong spell at Anfield. The Argentina midfielder is tied to Liverpool until 2028, yet there has still been no movement on improved terms. That has kept attention on his long term future, particularly after he previously admitted his disappointment at not being offered a new deal during the summer. Mac Allister has now reiterated that little has changed. Speaking to Sky Sports about what he could say regarding the next step in his career, he said: “Not much to be honest. “The situation didn’t change, but there’s a new sporting director, and there is new ownership coming into the club. So everything can happen and we will see whether it’s this season or next season. We will see what happens. “But right now I’m just enjoying my football, enjoying playing for this amazing club that is one of the best in the world. And we will see. We will see in the future what happens.” Photo: IMAGO Mac Allister contract remains unresolved Those comments are unlikely to quieten speculation entirely. Mac Allister remains one of Liverpool’s most important midfielders and his level under Andoni Iraola has reinforced the feeling that his current standing deserves to be reflected in a new agreement. There is no suggestion of an immediate exit, but the absence of progress leaves space for uncertainty. That matters when a player of his pedigree continues to attract elite interest across Europe. Liverpool future shaped by summer decisions Manchester City were among the clubs linked during the last transfer window, and his profile has only strengthened since then. Across 13 appearances in all competitions this season, Mac Allister has contributed four goals and one assist, numbers that underline his influence from midfield. Since arriving from Brighton in 2023, he has recorded 23 goals and 21 assists in 163 appearances for Liverpool. Those figures reflect consistency as much as quality, and explain why rival clubs continue to monitor developments. Transfer interest likely if no new deal emerges Liverpool will be aware that extending Mac Allister’s contract would send a clear message. If no agreement is reached in the coming months, his situation is likely to feature prominently again ahead of next summer. For now, the message from the player is measured and calm. He remains focused on his football, but the wider picture around the Alexis Mac Allister contract and his Liverpool future is still open.

item.title: Liverpool boss Andoni Iraola brushes off Jamie Carragher title talk ahead of Arsenal showdown
item.description: Liverpool v Chelsea - Carabao Cup Fourth Round - Getty Images Sport Andoni Iraola has dismissed Jamie Carragher's suggestion that Liverpool are the primary challengers for the Premier League title this season. The manager insisted it is far too early for such discussions as he prepares his squad for a crucial clash against Arsenal at Anfield on Sunday. Iraola dismisses early title chatter Iraola has firmly played down suggestions that his Liverpool side are the main challengers for the Premier League title. Former defender Carragher recently claimed the Merseyside club should be considered the primary threat to Arsenal at the top of the table this season. Liverpool have responded superbly to a heavy 3-0 defeat against Manchester City earlier this month. They have secured five consecutive victories across all competitions to bounce back in style, including an impressive triumph over Brighton last weekend. Writing in The Telegraph , Carragher suggested that a victory over Arsenal at Anfield would firmly establish their title credentials. He noted this is particularly relevant given the ongoing uncertainty surrounding City following their recent guilty verdict . Liverpool boss focuses on Arsenal test Despite the growing external hype and positive results, Iraola is refusing to get carried away by the recent run of good form. The manager insists his complete focus remains on the immediate challenge of facing Arsenal on Sunday. "I think it is too early to start looking at the standings," Iraola explained to the media during his pre-match press conference. "It is about preparing ourselves for a very difficult game. We know Arsenal and how good they are. They have very good players, working a lot in synchronicity and we have to be ready for that challenge." Halfway mark remains the true gauge The Liverpool manager believes the league table will only provide an accurate reflection of their genuine prospects much later in the campaign. He stressed that his squad still has plenty of room for development and tactical growth. "It is still October," Iraola continued. "We have to take one game at a time and I always say the reference is more or less when we've played against each other once, so halfway through the season. That’s when you can start to look at the standings. "Right now, we are in a position where we need to improve and keep getting better. For fans, it is good if they have expectations or they think we can win, normally that's a good thing, but if you ask me I think it is still very early in the season." Injury boosts ahead of Anfield showdown Liverpool will hope to use the notoriously vibrant Anfield atmosphere to their advantage when they host Arsenal this Sunday. The Reds could also receive a significant double fitness boost ahead of the weekend clash. Dominik Szoboszlai and Víctor Munoz are both continuing their respective recoveries from hamstring and knee injuries, with the club hoping they can return to action on Sunday.

item.title: Patriots legend admits Rob Gronkowski influenced his decision to extend Patriots career
item.description: Photo by Kevin C. Cox/Getty Images Matt Light has revealed that Rob Gronkowski played a part in convincing him to delay retirement and spend another season with the New England Patriots. The former Patriots offensive tackle had considered hanging up his boots after his 10th NFL season but changed his mind after developing a close bond with the legendary tight end. Light ultimately stayed for another campaign, giving him more time alongside Gronkowski during their run together in New England. Matt Light reveals why he wanted another season with Rob Gronkowski Speaking on NBC Sports Boston, Light explained that Gronkowski’s arrival influenced his decision to continue playing. “After my 10th season, you know, and feeling very fortunate to spend my entire career in New England, and I was thinking about hanging it up, but that was my first year with Gronk, and I thought, you know what, man, I gotta have at least one more with this cat,” Light said. He admitted that several factors contributed to his decision, but spending more time with Gronkowski was certainly among them. “That’s a fact. I mean, look, there were other things that went into it, but that was definitely a thought process, and I’m so glad I did. I mean, you know, look, we didn’t win it all that year, but we came as close as you can get, and it was a special time. I mean, I got a lot of great memories, you know, being with him is one of them.” Gronkowski joined the Patriots in 2010 after being selected 42nd overall in the NFL Draft. Light, who had been drafted nine years earlier, helped the young tight end adjust to life in the league. Gronkowski later acknowledged that support, explaining how Light took him under his wing and taught him aspects of playing in the run game. Their relationship extended beyond football, with the pair sharing experiences away from the field and maintaining their friendship after Light retired. The offensive tackle eventually stepped away from the NFL in 2012, following the Patriots’ Super Bowl XLVI defeat to the New York Giants. Light cited the physical demands of the game and the growing difficulty of recovering as he got older, explaining that football was leaving him with little energy for his family. Their connection remains strong. With Gronkowski set to enter the Patriots Hall of Fame, the pair have joined forces for a sweepstakes supporting their respective charities, the Light Foundation and the Gronk Nation Youth Foundation. item.description: Numbers show 32-year-old star’s growing importance to Real Madrid under Jose Mourinho after a slow start Real Madrid have seen their performances improve in recent weeks following Jose Mourinho’s tactical tweaks. The team looks much better organised defensively and has also gained more balance and control in midfield following the changes. One player who is helping Madrid achieve that control, especially in midfield, is Portuguese midfielder Bernardo Silva. A remarkable statistic helps underline his importance. Excluding El Clasico , Real Madrid average 57% possession with Bernardo on the pitch. The number drops to just 47% in games where the former Manchester City star is absent. In that 10% difference lies Real Madrid’s control. Bernardo Silva transforming Madrid’s midfield control The numbers clearly indicate that Madrid see more of the ball in games where Bernardo Silva is involved. His greatest strength has never simply been passing the ball accurately. It is his ability to drop deep to receive the ball, take possession under pressure and escape tight situations. Bernardo Silva has emerged as one of Real Madrid’s most important players in recent weeks. Against Barcelona, this quality was on display, especially in the first half, when Bernardo repeatedly picked out Yan Diomande’s runs from defensive midfield. For a Madrid side that has many direct players in their ranks, having someone like Bernardo can be the perfect calming influence. It is very similar to how Toni Kroos provided control, which allowed the rest of Madrid’s attack to thrive and score goals. item.description: BENGALURU: Women’s cricket in India has had its share of twists and turns. Its journey into Test cricket was no different. Although cricket had been introduced in the country much earlier, the first women’s national championship was held only in April 1973. The game was still finding its feet, with teams playing two and three-day red-ball matches. An Australian team toured India in 1975, and in February the following year, India travelled to New Zealand for a five-match ‘Test series’, which was subsequently deemed unofficial. The first women’s Test, between Australia and England, had been played in Brisbane in 1934. India had to wait another 42 years to make its official debut. That moment unfolded at the KSCA Stadium (renamed the M Chinnaswamy Stadium in 1987), when India hosted West Indies in the first of a six-Test series in October 1976. Led by Louise Browne, the visiting side took on Shantha Rangaswamy’s India in a three-day contest that began on October 31. For the women cricketers, it was a landmark moment. Recalling the occasion, Shantha said: “We had already played a couple of series against Australia and New Zealand, which were later deemed unofficial. So, we weren’t sure until later whether this match would count as an official one.” With one section of the stadium under renovation, the remaining stands were packed, with more than 22,000 spectators turning up. India’s line-up featured some of the rising stars of the game, including Diana Edulji, Shubhangi Kulkarni and Ujwala Nikam. Among those soaking in the atmosphere was former Indian wicketkeeper Kalpana Venkatachar, then a Karnataka age-group cricketer. She was part of a group of young women cricketers who volunteered at the match, handing out scorecards to spectators. “Back in the day, spectators also did the scoring. They watched, tracked and recorded every ball and run in a booklet provided to them. Our job was to hand out these booklets. The excitement was infectious and the crowd was boisterous,” Kalpana recalled. West Indies, who batted first, were bowled out for 274 in 78.4 overs. Shubhangi, one of India’s finest spinners, returned figures of 5/48, while Diana picked up two wickets. India’s reply produced two memorable knocks. Opener Shobha Pandit scored 69, but it was skipper Shantha’s gritty 74 that stole the show. Her innings also featured a landmark moment — a six over long-on off Patricia Whittaker, the first maximum by an Indian woman in international cricket and the first at the stadium. The stand where the ball landed has since been named after Shantha. She remembers the innings as an attempt to inject a modern-day T20 flavour into a game that was still played over three days. “With the matches being held over three days, most of them would end in draws.
